title: Tenant-aware dynamic concurrency controller for embedding and reranking endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware dynamic concurrency controller that adapts per-tenant concurrency limits, queue scheduling, and throttling to improve 99th-percentile latency and utilization for embedding and reranking endpoints while preventing noisy-neighbor behavior.
background: We have observed that a small number of tenants with bursty embedding/rerank workloads drive spikes that cause global autoscalers to overprovision or oscillate. Existing per-pool autoscaling responds too slowly to microbursts, and naive rate limits hurt latency-sensitive tenants. Recent incidents (INC-2025-09-17-embeddings-outage) showed cascading queue growth and degraded 99p latency for multi-tenant pools. We need a controller that works with queue shaping, token-bucket rate limits and predictive headroom to stabilize latency and cost.
goals: Reduce 99th-percentile per-request latency for embeddings/rerank by 25% for median tenants
Prevent more than 2 sustained autoscale oscillations per 24h window per pool
Maintain or reduce monthly GPU cost for the affected pools by intelligent packing and headroom reuse
Provide visibility and controls per-tenant (soft concurrency, burst tokens, priority class)
technical_solution: Introduce a controller component that runs alongside the existing router: (1) maintain per-tenant concurrency tokens derived from SLO class and historical QPS plus burst allowance; (2) perform request admission using a weighted fair queue that considers request size (embedding dims and number of vectors) and latency SLO; (3) feed short-term load forecasts (5s-60s) from the new lightweight predictor into autoscaler as a candidate headroom signal; (4) expose tenant controls via the Console and API: soft_concurrency, burst_window, priority_class; (5) integrate with existing metrics (prometheus) and autoscaler to avoid double-counting capacity requests. The controller will prefer shaping (queueing + prioritization) over hard rejects, and fall back to graceful 429 with Retry-After when overload is sustained.
acceptance_criteria: Canary experiment showing >=20% reduction in 99p latency for target tenants vs baseline over one week
No increase in 95p latency for low-latency SLO tenants during canary
Autoscaler stability: measured oscillations per pool <=2 in 7 days post-rollout
Operational dashboards show per-tenant concurrency usage and burst credit balance
Feature gate to disable controller per-pool or per-tenant
Runbook updated and tested with a simulated tenant burst scenario
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests for admission controller logic (local and staging)
Phase 1: Deploy controller in staging; run synthetic burst tests and validate metrics
Phase 2: Canary on a single low-risk pool with 5 pilot tenants for 72 hours
Phase 3: Expand canary to 30% of traffic with automated rollback criteria
Phase 4: Full rollout to all multi-tenant embedding pools with gradual enablement per-pool
Abort criteria: sustained 5%+ increase in 95p latency for any SLO-class tenant or autoscaler errors >1/hour
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Controller misconfiguration could starve low-priority tenants. Mitigation: start with permissive defaults and soft limits; require explicit opt-in to strict priority classes.
Risk: Predictor provides noisy signals causing autoscaler thrash. Mitigation: use smoothing + cooldown windows; autoscaler treats predictor as advisory signal only.
Risk: Increased operational complexity. Mitigation: Console views + alerting; oncall training and updated runbook.
Risk: Unexpected cost increase from headroom allocation. Mitigation: simulate cost impact using historical traces and enforce cost delta thresholds before global rollout.
dependencies: PM-419 (tenant pricing and priority tiers finalization)
DES-174 (Console UI for tenant concurrency controls)
notes: Early results in staging show the controller reduces short tail queue spikes but requires tuning of burst_window per tenant pattern.
We will run a A/B reranking quality check to ensure shaping doesn't materially change ranking quality under timeouts.
Owner: Marco will coordinate with PM and Design for Console controls; SRE to validate autoscaler integration.
